body.rationale: IPS status per the brief: ratified, so the hard breaches are binding. Ranking: (1) resampled_efficient_frontier has no hard breaches, the highest effective N among compliant candidates (13.1), the best compliant return (6.98%), and a Sharpe of 0.42. Resampling averages out CMA estimation error, which suits a regime where covariance structure deserves more trust than point forecasts. Its weakness is a backtest drawdown of -24.84% against the -25% limit. That is fragile, but it is still inside the limit. (2) tail_risk_parity uses downside co-movement only and reads no return forecasts. It has a low drawdown (-20.9%) and a CRO risk score of 0.42. Its volatility breach is small (7.67% vs the 8% floor) and is fixable by blending, though the intra-category reviewer rightly notes that semicovariance is not a true tail measure. (3) black_litterman is compliant with a 0.42 Sharpe and a -21.9% drawdown. The reviewers' point that ETF AUM double-counts overlapping equity sleeves in the prior distorts its implied returns, so it ranks below the covariance-based methods. (4) inverse_volatility is compliant, simple and forecast-free. It ignores correlation, and about 43% of the book sits in credit-like sleeves that fall together. (5) risk_parity has a 0.41 CRO score and a -20.3% drawdown, but its 7.56% volatility breaches the floor and the reviewers note it overstates risk diversification by reading capital-weight entropy as risk dispersion. My first choice beats my fifth because resampled_efficient_frontier clears every hard IPS limit and carries higher return and breadth, while risk_parity breaches volatility and offers less return. The bottom flag is market_cap_weight: it has a -40.6% drawdown that the CRO treats as a floor, a 0.80 risk score, and a breach of the ratified drawdown limit. It is also near-pure US equity beta, and reviewers noted that ETF AUM is not a market portfolio and double-counts overlapping style funds. The CIO should not lean on it. I did not flag adversarial_diversifier because its orthogonality has ensemble value, though I left it unranked given its three hard breaches.
